content_voiceover: This slide adds factor eight to the initiation phase diagram. The extrinsic tenase on the left is now shown faded, because TFPI has largely shut it down. On the right, factor eight, shown entering from outside the cell, gets activated by the thrombin generated below, becoming factor eight a. Factor eight a then combines with factor nine a on the membrane to form the intrinsic tenase complex, alongside factor ten, labeled here. This intrinsic tenase is now colored in and fully active, and it generates a fresh supply of factor ten a, shown diffusing down to feed the prothrombinase complex together with factor five a and prothrombin, producing more thrombin, factor two a. Notice the full feedback loop, thrombin activates factor five and factor eight, and those cofactors build the two key enzyme complexes, intrinsic tenase and prothrombinase, that together generate the explosive burst of thrombin seen in propagation.
keypoints: Thrombin activates factor eight to eight a via feedback
Factor eight a plus nine a forms the intrinsic tenase complex
Intrinsic tenase generates far more ten a than the extrinsic tenase alone
Combined intrinsic tenase and prothrombinase drive the thrombin burst
keypoint_voiceover: Factor eight a is the missing piece for intrinsic tenase, eight a plus nine a on the membrane. That complex churns out ten a far faster than tissue factor seven a ever could, feeding prothrombinase and producing the thrombin burst that defines propagation.
